nodes.name: Ni mesh cleaning
nodes.procedure: The NM (1 × 2 cm²) was submerged in 3 M HCl for 20 min to remove the surface oxides. Then, the surface residual HCl was removed by ultrasonication in deionized water three times.
nodes.source_text: The NM (1 × 2 cm²) was submerged in 3 M HCl for 20 min to remove the surface oxides. Then, the surface residual HCl was removed by ultrasonication in deionized water three times.

nodes.name: PN electrodeposition on NM
nodes.procedure: The cleaned NM was taken as the cathode and the high-purity nickel rod (99.5 wt.%) was used as the anode. The electrodeposition solution was a mixture of 0.15 M NiCl₂·6H₂O and 2 M NH₄Cl. Electrodeposition was operated at room temperature for 10 min at a current density of 1000 mA cm⁻². Porous Ni (PN) loading on NM is 86.5 mg cm⁻² (NM/PN).

nodes.procedure: Continuously, 0.21 M FeCl₂·4H₂O and 0.6 M H₃BO₃ were added into the solution and the solution was heated to 60°C. Next, NM/PN was maintained for 20 min at a deposition current density of 30 mA cm⁻².

nodes.name: PtNi electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: A continuous electrodeposition method was used to fabricate NM/PN/NiFeOₓ/PtNi. Briefly, a mixed solution containing 2.44 × 10⁻³ M (Pt²⁺) and 7.32 × 10⁻³ M (Ni²⁺) was used as the electrolyte and NM/PN/NiFeOₓ as the cathode. The electro-deposition was carried out at room temperature for 240 s with a current density of 10 mA cm⁻².

nodes.evidence_snippet: Pore structure of NM/PN/NiFeOx electrode is characterized by static mercury pressure testing, as shown in Figure 1f, which possess a multi-stage porous structure with the average pore size of 45.8 μm , and large pores with 63.3 and 145.0 μm originate from Ni mesh itself.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p peaks show Ni2+ at 850.8 eV (2p3/2) and 869.2 eV (2p1/2), Ni0 at 849.7 eV (2p3/2) and 867.3 eV (2p1/2), satellites at 855.4 and 873.4 eV for oxidized Ni suggesting NiO and Ni(OH)2. Fe 2p peaks show Fe0 at 706.5 and 719.6 eV, Fe3+ at 711.3 eV (2p3/2) and 724.6 eV (2p1/2).
nodes.evidence_snippet: XPS analysis in Figure 2b-d show the Ni and Fe valence state information of NiFeOx , respectively. The Ni2p main peak is decomposed into two valence states for samples containing Ni2+ (850.8 eV Ni2p3/2 and 869.2 eV Ni2p1/2 ) and Ni0 (849.7 eV Ni2p3/2 and 867.3 eV Ni2p1/2 ). As shown in Figure 2c, peaks at 855.4 and 873.4 eV correspond to the satellites of Ni2p3/2 and Ni2p1/2 in oxidized Ni, respectively, suggesting the occurrence of NiO and Ni(OH)2 . In the Fe2p XPS spectrum (Figure 2d), two peaks around 706.5 and 719.6 eV belong to Fe2p3/2 and Fe2p1/2 of Fe0 , and higher oxidized Fe3+ oxidation state reflect peaks at 711.3 ( Fe2p3/2 ) and 724.6 eV ( Fe2p1/2 ), indicating that the presence of Fe0 and Fe3+.

nodes.evidence_snippet: The amorphous layer (≈5 nm thickness) on the surface of NiFeOx nano-cone is observed clearly by high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM), as shown in Figure 2e.
